title: TDD->Build scope gate: extend the construction-level file-scope advisory to multi-member lanes (cycle-1620 audit L3)
summary: The cycle-1620 salvage made multi-member lanes reconcile the TDD handoff's declared member set against the contract's bound set (fatal on mismatch) and return before the single-member tail, so the cycle-1111 construction-level check — authored test files vs the committed item's declared scope (fileScopeAdvisory) — no longer runs for lanes with two or more members. Label drift is legitimately superseded by set equality there; the file-scope advisory is not.
root_cause: topngate.tddScopeGate.check: the multi-member branch (reconcileMemberSets) returns early; fileScopeAdvisory is keyed on a single claimed slug and a single committed item's declared scope.
fix: Union readScoutTargetFiles over every committed member and run one overlap check of the authored files against that union, advisory only (block=false), after a complete multi-member reconciliation; keep single-member behavior byte-identical.
acceptance: A complete two-member declaration whose authored files lie outside both members' declared scopes yields the file-scope advisory (block=false) with both members named.
A complete two-member declaration whose authored files lie inside either member's scope yields no advisory.
Single-member lanes keep today's advisory text and behavior; go vet + topngate suite + -race green.
connects_to: multi-slug-lane-scope-reconciliation (consumed 2026-09-10 — the salvage that opened this gap)
notes: Filed from the salvage's architecture review (MEDIUM, documented follow-up). Advisory-only: no ship risk, so it sits below the pipeline-integrity band.
